findings.explanation: The Splunk Universal Forwarder is downloaded from splunk.com, not Splunkbase, and it has no SNMP polling input; splunkbase.splunk.com/app/617 returns 404.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Name the actual SNMP collector: Splunk Connect for SNMP or the SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase 1537), polling PowerNet-MIB rPDU2OutletMeteredStatusCurrent. Drop the Universal Forwarder and the 617 ID.

findings.explanation: SC4SNMP writes polling events as sourcetype sc4snmp:event to index netops by default, while the spl expects sourcetype snmp:apc:pdu in index=power with flat pdu_name and outlet_id fields. Nothing explains the override. The repository guide uses sourcetype snmp:pdu / snmp:rpdu.
findings.quote: Splunk Connect for SNMP (SC4SNMP) or SNMP Modular Input
findings.suggested_fix: Document how sourcetype snmp:apc:pdu, pdu_name and the outlet index are produced, or align with the guide's sourcetype.

findings.explanation: The search is a 7-day hourly trend with no alert condition, and '-7d' is the lookback window, not a threshold. 'Title terms' is a word list standing in for an explanation.
findings.quote: Alert logic enforces -7d. Title terms: APC, PDU, SNMP, Per, Outlet.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe it as a report: hourly average current per outlet over the last 7 days, used to spot step changes and outlets nearing their rating.

findings.explanation: Title words are pasted in where the value statement should be; it says nothing about what per-outlet trending is good for.
findings.quote: helps teams contain APC, PDU, SNMP, Per, Outlet scenarios
findings.suggested_fix: State the value: per-outlet current trends show which servers drive rack power growth, catch unexpected step changes after installs, and support chargeback and capacity planning.

findings.explanation: The 0.1 A scaling is correct for rPDU2OutletMeteredStatusCurrent. However, the text doesn't say that only outlet-metered PDUs expose per-outlet current (switched-only outlets have no current column), and it asks for step-change alerting that the SPL does not implement.
findings.quote: (1) Confirm MIB scaling (0.1 A units). (2) Label outlets in DCIM. (3) Alert on step changes after installs.
findings.suggested_fix: State that per-outlet current requires an outlet-metered model (rPDU2OutletMeteredStatusTable), and describe the step-change alert as a separate search to build (for example, comparing the hourly average with the prior 7-day baseline).

findings.explanation: The spl is a 7-day trend report (earliest=-7d) with no alert rows, so the 24-hour schedule and paging throttle don't apply. The HEC and vendor-API troubleshooting doesn't apply to SNMP polling either.
findings.quote: Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. ... inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint
findings.suggested_fix: Describe saving it as a dashboard or report over 7 days. Replace the REST/HEC troubleshooting with SNMP polling checks (credentials, UDP 161, MIB loading, per-outlet table walk size).

findings.explanation: These are template scenarios: 'elevates outlet' is meaningless and there is no threshold. They don't describe real causes of misleading per-outlet trends.
findings.quote: Batch `avg` on `snmp:apc:pdu` — Scheduled automation elevates `outlet` without crossing configured threshold
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: outlets renumbered or relabelled after PDU replacement, server power-supply failover shifting load between A and B feeds, missing polls showing as dips, and firmware that reports 0 A for very low loads.

findings.explanation: The SPL uses non-existent MIB columns and an invalid timechart split, so it cannot have run successfully.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft or unverified until an SME runs it.

findings.explanation: SC4SNMP is not distributed through Splunkbase.
findings.suggested_fix: Link https://splunk.github.io/splunk-connect-for-snmp/ and the PowerNet-MIB rPDU2OutletMeteredStatusTable definition.

findings.explanation: The trend uses polled values, not traps.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: rPDU2OutletMeteredStatusLoad and rPDU2OutletSwitchedStatusLoad are not PowerNet-MIB objects. The per-outlet current column is rPDU2OutletMeteredStatusCurrent (tenths of amps), and rPDU2OutletSwitchedStatusTable has no current column (https://oidref.com/1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.26.9.4.3.1, https://oidref.com/1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.26.9.2.3.1). outletIndex is also not an object name (the index is rPDU2OutletMeteredStatusIndex/Number).

'timechart span=1h avg(amps) by pdu_name outlet' is invalid: timechart accepts a single split-by field (https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/Timechart). Combine the fields first, for example eval series=pdu_name.":".outlet, then split by series.
The title says 'Power Draw', but the SPL trends current in amps. Watts are available as rPDU2OutletMeteredStatusPower if power is intended.

summary: A per-outlet current trend whose SPL reads non-existent PowerNet-MIB columns and uses an invalid two-field timechart split. The prose is title-word salad with an alert condition ('-7d') that the search does not have.
